source.title: Unleashing the Unseen: Harnessing Benign Datasets for Jailbreaking Large Language Models
source.authors: Wei Zhao; Zhe Li; Yi-Ge Li; Junfeng Sun

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance and whether suffixes can bypass safety, using custom benign datasets, extracted suffixes, and ASR rather than the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: Reports ASR for harmful prompts after benign fine-tuning and with suffix attacks, so those results are recorded. It does not measure per-token KL, compliant prefilling, decoding changes, or whether safety is localized in weights. Format-transferability results and harmfulness scores are not separate rows because ASR is the reported direct measure of harmful compliance.
record.test_reason: Measures harmful-prompt ASR after fine-tuning five aligned models on benign datasets (V2). It also measures ASR when optimized suffixes (benign-derived and harmful-derived) are appended to AdvBench prompts (V4, suffix part). Methods differ from the originals: custom style datasets, soft-prompt suffix extraction, GPT-4-turbo judge.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that benign features can act as adversarial suffixes. They also conclude that suffixes from jailbreak-style optimization carry meaningful features, and that benign datasets with dominant features can erode safety through fine-tuning, even on GPT models via the API. They argue benign fine-tuning cannot be assumed to preserve safety.
record.recipe_differences: Uses fine-tuning on custom benign style/format datasets and suffix-based attacks; reports ASR and harmfulness rather than reproducing the original fine-tuning recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Effects vary by model, dataset or suffix type, and suffix representation (token versus embedding); Poem features have little effect on some strongly aligned models, while Structure features often have large effects.

fits_no_version.finding: PCC between last hidden states shows successful suffixes dominate the prompt's representation (e.g., Structure suffix PCC_Hs = 0.78; Poem suffix PCC_Hp = 0.95).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Jailbreak success tracks how much a suffix, rather than the prompt, determines the final hidden state.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The benign fine-tuning results vary by model and dataset; several reported degradations are small. Fine-tuning duration differs between open-source and closed-source models.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for transferability or harmfulness-score columns in Tables 1–3 and 5; ASR is the direct harmful-compliance measure retained. Figure 5 also summarizes suffix performance, with table results recorded where available.

untested.parts: No per-token KL or position-wise analysis; the PCC on last hidden states is not a token-depth measure.
Prefilling a compliant start and decoding changes are not tested; only suffixes.
No test of whether data or objective causes token-level shallowness. The authors suggest models 'overlearn' dominant features, but this is not tested against depth.
No varying of dataset size, steps or epochs. Open models get 2000 steps, GPT models 3 epochs, and this difference is not controlled.

missing.what: ASR and harmfulness for the Repeat Response and Basic Programming embedding suffixes extracted from harmful data. Values are shown in a bar chart; the model is not clearly specified.

record.verdict_notes: The claim of 'completely eliminating' GPT safety rests on the Structure and BASIC datasets (99%+ ASR on GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o). No uncertainty estimates or repeated runs are reported. ASR is judged by GPT-4-turbo. The study's evidence is consistent with shallow safety in general but does not test token depth.

versions.untested_parts: The fine-tuning datasets in this study are benign; it does not test fine-tuning on harmful examples.
Does not test every kind of ordinary or carefully selected benign data; fine-tunes on the specific datasets described.
No per-token KL measurement between aligned and base models.
Tests suffix attacks, not compliant prefilling or decoding changes.
No weight or rank localization tests.
Does not test why safety behaviour is shallow or whether data or objective causes token-position shallowness.
Does not test training to spread safety beyond the first tokens or the durability of such training.

tranche.reason: Custom benign-format fine-tuning and feature-extracted token or embedding suffixes test V2 and V4 through methods differing from the original recipes.

source_check.notes: Llama3-guard is the paper's own ambiguous model designation; its exact checkpoint and size are unspecified. Repeat and BASIC data use harmful-derived suffixes on benign prompts followed by GPT-4 filtering, unlike the template-generated Structure and Poem data.
